implementation_notes: Default realization: a module-scoped Map keyed by string (or symbol) with register/lookup exported from the module; types are carried by a generic Factory<T> signature at the registration site. It replaces the Registry class with module scope and keeps lookup synchronous.
pitfalls: Generics are erased: lookup<T> asserts a type nothing checks at runtime, so a mismatched key/type pair only fails downstream - use an InjectionToken<T>-style token object that carries the type when the key domain is worth the ceremony.

Duplicate module instances (dual ESM/CJS builds, multiple copies in node_modules, different bundler chunks) each get their own Map, so registrations silently vanish; keep the registry on a globalThis symbol if that must not happen.
The Map holds strong references for the process lifetime; key by object/symbol and use a WeakMap when entries should be collectable.

variants.name: decorator + reflect-metadata self-registration
variants.implementation_notes: Classes announce themselves: a class decorator writes the class (or a factory) into the module registry at definition time, with reflect-metadata providing the metadata the container reads back (TypeScript 5 standard decorators, or experimentalDecorators plus emitDecoratorMetadata). It replaces explicit registration calls, at the price of configuration and import-order coupling.
pitfalls: Decorators run only when the module is evaluated, so tree-shaking, dynamic imports or a bundler that drops 'unused' modules can make registrations disappear - the host must import plugin modules explicitly or scan for them.
Two decorator systems exist (legacy experimentalDecorators and TS 5 standard decorators) with different signatures and metadata behaviour; mixing them in one project produces run-time surprises.

reflect-metadata adds a global polyfill and decorator metadata is emitted only when emitDecoratorMetadata is on, so type-driven resolution silently degrades to undefined in alternative build setups (esbuild, SWC).
